title: How to Connect a Refrigerator Water and Ice Dispenser | This Old House

locations.name: Basement utility space under the stove area (evidence includes moving to basement to locate cold water line, mentions two floor holes and an abandoned hot water line).
locations.basis: Transcript explicitly moves to the basement and notes the stove area; mentions two holes in the floor and an abandoned hot water line near a cold-water line with a shut-off valve.

summary: This Old House walks through connecting a refrigerator’s water dispenser to a cold-water supply. The host locates the existing cold-water line and shut-off valve in the basement, identifies an abandoned hot-water line, and then demonstrates copper-pipe preparation, soldering a transition to a compression line, and attaching the refrigerator’s supply line. The process covers pipe cleaning, fluxing, a soldered copper joint, threading with Teflon tape, tightening with two wrenches, and finally testing the dispenser for flow.

sections.title: Assess fridge readiness and locate cold water supply
sections.description: The video opens with the host noting that the fridge is already ready internally and only needs a connection to a cold water line. The narrator then begins by locating the cold-water line and nearby plumbing access in the basement.

sections.title: Explore plumbing path and identify lines
concepts: cold water line with shut-off valve
sections.description: The host goes to the basement, observes two floor holes (originally for a washing machine), and identifies an abandoned hot-water line and a functional cold-water line with a shut-off valve, establishing feasibility for a connection.

sections.title: Prepare and cut copper pipe
sections.description: The copper pipe is prepared and cut with a tubing cutter, and the exposed surface is cleaned with Emery cloth to ensure proper solder adhesion.

sections.title: Soldering prep and initial joint setup
sections.description: The presenter explains fluxing both the pipe and the fitting to prepare for soldering, and emphasizes clean, uniform surfaces to ensure a good solder joint.

sections.title: Threading prep and compression connection setup
sections.description: Three wraps of Teflon tape are applied to the new fitting. The pipe is threaded into the fitting and aligned for tightening, with emphasis on avoiding cross-threading and ensuring a straight orientation.

sections.title: Connect supply line and test the dispenser
sections.description: The supply line is connected to the refrigerator using a ground joint fitting with a light sealant, tightened with two wrenches, and the water is turned back on. The dispenser is then tested to confirm flow.

featured_techniques.technique: Identify cold water supply and shut-off valve in basement plumbing
Clean and prepare copper pipe surface with Emery cloth
Clean fitting with wire brush before assembly
Apply flux to pipe and fitting prior to solder
Solder copper joint using opposite-side heat to draw solder
Apply teflon tape (thread sealant) to threaded fitting
Thread and tighten new compression fitting with two wrenches
Install ground joint connection and sealant at supply line
Test refrigerator water dispenser for operation after connection
